title: WPMS/950/2011 of GURMUKH DASS Vs SRI BHARAT BHUSHAN WADHAWA

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
WRIT PETITION (M/S) NO.950 of 2011
Gurmukh Dass ... Petitioner
Vs.
Sri Bharat Bhushan Wadhawa ... Respondent
Advocate: Mr. Shailendra Singh Chauhan, learned counsel for the
petitioner.
Mr. Rajendra Singh Dobhal, learned Senior Counsel
assisted by Mr. G.D. Joshi, learned counsel for the
respondent.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
The petitioner before this Court is a
defendant in Suit No.256 of 2007 "Bharat Bhushan
Wadhawa Vs. Gurmukh Dass", which were the
proceedings drawn by the respondent-plaintiff
before the Court of Civil Judge (Junior Division),
Dehradun praying for the following reliefs:-

2. The suit proceeded. Notices were issued
and despite of the substitutive mode of service of
notice under Order 5 Rule 20 of the CPC, the
defendant had not put in appearance.
Consequently, the Court of Civil Judge (Junior
Division), Dehradun by the judgment of 21.02.2009
had decreed the suit.
3. At the stage of decreeing the suit, the
Court of Civil Judge (Junior Division), Dehradun has
recorded the finding that, a as per the notice issued
under Order 5 Rule 20 of the CPC, a satisfaction of
service was recorded and since none has appeared
despite service of notice nor any written statement
was filed, the suit was directed to proceed ex-parte
by an order of 21.02.2009.
4. The said order directing the suit to
proceed ex-parte on 21.02.2009 was never a
subject matter of challenge before any Court
seeking its recall for enabling the suit to be decided
on its merits.
5. In the absence of the defendants, in the
absence of the written statement and in the
absence of the recall of the order of 21.02.2009
directing the suit to proceed ex-parte, the Court
had no option except to decree the suit, based on
the pleadings raised by the plaintiff in the suit.
Accordingly, the following decree was rendered:-

6. The said decree rendered by the Court of
Civil Judge (Junior Division), Dehradun was put to
execution and it is contended by the defendant-petitioner that it is when the execution proceedings
were instituted, he could gathered the knowledge of
the ex-parte decree and thus he filed an application
under Order 9 Rule 13 of the CPC on 16.09.2010.
The said application was opposed by the respondent
and, consequently, application under Order 9 Rule
13 was rejected by the trial Court by order dated
13.12.2010, which upon being challenged under
Order 43 Rule 1(d) stood affirmed in Misc. Civil
Appeal No.116 of 2011 with dismissal of the appeal
by the judgment of 10.05.2011.
7. There are two folds arguments, which has
been raised by the learned counsel for the
petitioners as against the impugned orders:-
1) That the address of the defendant
given in the suit was not the exact
address of his abode and, hence, the
presumption would be that he was not
served with the notice;
2) He submits that the substitutive mode
of service of notice as adopted under

4
Order 5 Rule 20 of the CPC was not an
effective mode of service because the
newspaper 'Dainik Pradhan Times' in
which the publication was directed to be
made was not a newspaper of wide
circulation in the area. Hence, the
presumption would be that he was not
served with the notice.
8. In order to answer the two plea raised by
the learned counsel for the petitioner as against the
concurrent rejection of application under Order 9
Rule 13 of the CPC, a much vivid elaborate
consideration is not required to be made with
regard to the pleadings, for the reason being, that
the first argument pertaining to a wrong address
being given in the plaint could be answered
straightaway, for the reason being, that in the
application filed under Order 9 Rule 13 of the CPC,
that was the first available opportunity to the
defendant to have raised the aforesaid plea that the
notice could not be served because of the fact that
wrong address was given in the plaint.
9. In fact, in the absence of there being any
such specific plea taken, in the application under
Order 9 Rule 13 of the CPC, the said plea cannot be
permitted to be qualified by the defendant-petitioner at any subsequent stage of the
proceedings, including the proceedings under Order

5
43 of the CPC or even an extended proceedings of
the writ-petition under Article 227 of the
Constitution of India.
10. It needs no reference that the Writ Courts
have had to confine itself to the pleadings, which
were initially raised before the trial Court or the
Appellate Court and elaboration of pleadings, which
entails consideration of evidence could not be a
subject matter under Article 227 of the Constitution
of India, when it is exercising a supervisory
jurisdiction over the orders passed by the Sub-ordinate Courts, which itself means that it is the
scrutiny of the legal defects of the judgment
impugned in a writ-petition, which is a subject
matter of Article 227 of the Constitution of India
and it is not a scope where a new fact could be
pleaded for the first time, which was otherwise not
there before the learned Trial Court.
11. Thus, for the aforesaid reasons, the wrong
address being given in the plaint since not being a
ground or foundation for application under Order 9
Rule 13 of the CPC cannot be permitted to be
elaborated in his argument under Article 227 of the
Constitution of India. Thus, not acceptable.
12. Secondly, the learned counsel for the
petitioner submits that the substitutive mode of
service as adopted under the provisions of under
Order 5 Rule 20 of the CPC by issuing directions for

6
making publication in 'Dainik Pradhan Times', if that
publication has been effected upon, the
presumption would be that of service of notice on
the defendant-petitioner, that means the knowledge
of the pending proceedings and once the publication
itself is made, the plea of wrong address itself
becomes irrelevant.
13. It has been argued by the learned Senior
Counsel for the respondent that the plea of wrong
address being given in the suit is not acceptable for
the reason being that even in the affidavit filed in
support of the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of
the CPC by the defendant-petitioner, in fact, bears
the same address which has been given in the suit.
14. He submits that the newspaper, in which
the publication was made, was not a newspaper
which was of wide circulation. This plea could have
been considered, subject to a condition that there
would have a plea taken by the defendant-petitioner that the newspaper, in which the
publication was made, was not a newspaper notified
by the Court, in which the publication could be
made by substitutive mode of service under Order 5
Rule 20 of the CPC.
15. For the purpose of resorting to the
substitutive mode under Order 5 Rule 20 of the
CPC, each Court notifies a list of newspapers, in
which the publication is to be made. It is not a case

7
of the petitioner, at any stage, when the application
under Order 9 Rule 13 of the CPC was being
considered that the paper, in which the publication
was made, i.e. 'Dainik Pradhan Times' was not a
notified paper by the Courts, which could have, at
all, any bearing on the argument extended by the
learned counsel for the applicant.
16. Since, whatsoever has been attempted to
be argued by the counsel for the petitioner is
beyond the scope of the writ-petition or the
pleading raised before the Court below, the same
cannot be permitted to be ventured into for the first
time under Article 227 of the Constitution of India,
the writ-petition lacks merits and the same is,
accordingly, dismissed.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 03.07.2023
